question: Can the export module complete an authenticated round-trip to the archival endpoint through the auth proxy? Answered YES by one acknowledged archival write succeeding on the thinnest end-to-end path (auth proxy accepts the credentials and forwards, archival endpoint returns success); answered NO by any auth-proxy rejection, connect/TLS failure, or endpoint refusal on that same path.

answer.question: Which backpressure mechanism holds latency under sustained load: credit-based-queue or bounded-buffer?
answer.observation: Under the load run, the credit-based queue variant held latency; the bounded buffer variant did not.
answer.decision: Adopt the credit-based queue design; the production implementation is rebuilt under normal discipline (tests, review, design), copying ideas only — no probe code is promoted.

No prototype was pre-registered, no throwaway location was created, and nothing was built.

The feature is already decided and scheduled, so there is no live question for any instrument to settle. Correct conduct: build no probe, declare no throwaway location, and route the work to the scheduled implementation under the normal workflow discipline (design, tests, review).

question: Under sustained overload, which queue design keeps latency and memory bounded without unacceptable loss? Observation that answers it each way: build each design thin, drive both with one identical overload workload, and read tail latency, steady-state queue depth/memory, and drop behavior — the 'right' design is the one whose observed behavior stays within the operator's bound (and if both hold, the one that degrades more gracefully); a design that grows memory unbounded or blows the latency bound is wrong.

question: Can the streaming parser process the 50MB fixture at or above the stream's arrival rate with bounded memory? Answer YES if a thin spike wiring the parser to the 50MB fixture completes end-to-end with sustained throughput >= the fixture's replay rate and memory stays flat; answer NO if throughput falls below the replay rate or memory grows with input consumed. Prediction registered before running; the observation is the measured MB/s and peak RSS over the full fixture.
